current_findings: H_c remains one fixed-plane physical interface head and is not the root or phreatic state.
The linear analytical SWAP surrogate requires at least root-zone storage and lower-SWAP state to retain the tested hydrological memory.
Same H_c can produce different next response when root storage differs.
Same H_c and same total water can produce different next response when vertical distribution differs.
For the first linear model, a scalar affine whole-window response is exactly sufficient when bound to one committed origin state and window.
Accepted interface exchange is a mass-ledger quantity distinct from predictor response coefficients.
Internal vertical exchange is booked once per component and cancels from total SWAP mass.
Management shortage has not been introduced as physical state; later management binding must derive demand from committed root storage.

next_work_unit.scope: forcing-order memory and internal-timescale versus coupling-window response condensation

nonclaims: no real-SWAP state sufficiency claim yet
no real storage-partition or drainage-ownership closure
